name: PolyMATH
intro: PolyMath是一个多语言数学推理基准，涵盖18种语言和4个难度级别。该基准旨在评估大型语言模型在多语言环境下的数学推理能力，并揭示了LLM在多语言推理中的关键挑战。它通过确保难度全面性、语言多样性和高质量翻译，成为一个具有高度区分度的多语言数学基准。研究发现，即使是先进的LLM也仅能达到约50%的准确率。
build_method: 专家难度标注, GPT-4o预翻译, 数学术语提取, 语言专家校准
eval_feature: 18种平行语言, 四档难度各125题, 专家翻译校准, 规则答案匹配, 难度权重1/2/4/8
build_method_en: Expert difficulty labeling, GPT-4o pretranslation, math-term extraction, language-expert calibration
eval_feature_en: 18 parallel languages, 125 problems per difficulty level, expert translation calibration, rule-based answer matching, 1/2/4/8 difficulty weights
intro_en: PolyMath is a multilingual mathematical reasoning benchmark covering 18 languages and 4 difficulty levels. It aims to evaluate large language models' mathematical reasoning abilities in a multilingual context and highlights key challenges LLMs face in multilingual reasoning. By ensuring comprehensive difficulty, language diversity, and high-quality translations, it serves as a highly discriminative multilingual math benchmark. Studies show that even advanced LLMs achieve only about 50% accuracy.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2504.18428v4 dataset-construction, translation, and evaluation sections plus the official QwenLM/PolyMath repository. PolyMATH contains 500 original English problems total, not 500 per level: 125 are assigned to each of four levels defined by thought depth and knowledge breadth. Sources include MGSM, official examinations and competitions, and 25 HLE problems at the top level. A mathematics expert assigns each level and two additional experts confirm every tag. GPT-4o pretranslates the same problems into 17 target languages; math experts extract key terms; language experts with mathematics knowledge calibrate terminology, formulas, logical equivalence, and fluency. The 18 parallel languages yield 9,000 instances and cover about 75% of native speakers. Models return boxed answers. Non-reasoning open models use greedy decoding; reasoning models use temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, and 16 runs per sample for average@16. A human-validated rule matcher exceeds 98% precision. Difficulty-Weighted Accuracy uses weights 1, 2, 4, and 8 across the four levels, alongside language, level, and consistency analyses.
